sentences.zh: ○苗晉卿裴冕裴遵慶子向向子寅寅子樞=苗晉卿=苗晉卿，上黨壺關人。

translations.literal: ○ Miao Jinqing, Pei Mian, Pei Zunqing, Zi Xiang, Xiang's son Yin, Yin's son Shu = Miao Jinqing = Miao Jinqing, a native of Huguan in Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: ○ Biographies: Miao Jinqing; Pei Mian; Pei Zunqing; his son Zi Xiang; Zi Xiang's son Yin; Yin's son Shu. — Miao Jinqing was a native of Huguan in Shangdang commandery.

sentences.zh: 世以儒素稱。

translations.literal: His family for generations was known for Confucian simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: His clan was renowned for scholarly rectitude.

sentences.zh: 祖夔，高道不仕，追贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kui, of lofty character and did not take office, was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kui, a man of lofty principles who never entered government service, was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 父殆庶，官至絳州龍門縣丞，早卒，以晉卿贈太子少保。

translations.literal: His father Dai Shu reached the office of Assistant Magistrate of Longmen County in Jiang Prefecture, died early, and because of Jinqing was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dai Shu rose to assistant magistrate of Longmen County in Jiang Prefecture and died young; on account of Jinqing's eminence he was posthumously granted the title Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 晉卿幼好學，善屬文，進士擢第。

translations.literal: Jinqing from youth loved learning, was skilled at literary composition, and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Jinqing devoted himself to study, excelled at composition, and qualified as a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 初授懷州修武縣尉，歷奉先縣尉，坐累貶徐州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed Sheriff of Xiuwu County in Huai Prefecture, served as Sheriff of Fengxian, and because of accumulated offenses was demoted to Registrar of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was first appointed sheriff of Xiuwu in Huai Prefecture, later served as sheriff of Fengxian, then was demoted to registrar of Xuzhou on account of implicated misconduct.

sentences.zh: 秩滿隨調，判入高等，授萬年縣尉。

translations.literal: When his term ended he followed the regular reassignment; his examination papers were graded in the highest category, and he was appointed Sheriff of Wannian County.
translations.idiomatic: Upon completing his term he entered the routine transfer process, received top marks on his evaluation, and was appointed sheriff of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史，歷度支、兵、吏部三員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attending Censor and successively served as Vice Director in the Ministries of Revenue, War, and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to attendant censor and served in succession as vice director in the ministries of revenue, war, and personnel.

sentences.zh: 開元二十三年，遷吏部郎中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 23 (735) he was promoted to director within the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，與吏部郎中孫逖並拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he and Sun Ti, Director in the Ministry of Personnel, were jointly appointed Drafting Attendants in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he and Sun Ti were both appointed drafting attendants of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，以本官權知吏部選事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, while retaining his existing office, he was temporarily charged with managing the Ministry of Personnel selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 27 he was assigned, while retaining his rank, to oversee civil-service examinations and appointments.

sentences.zh: 晉卿性謙柔，選人有訴訟索好官者，雖至數千言，或聲色甚厲者，晉卿必含容之，略無慍色。

translations.literal: Jinqing's nature was humble and gentle; when candidates came with lawsuits seeking good offices, even if they spoke thousands of words or their voice and expression were very fierce, Jinqing would always tolerate them, with scarcely any sign of anger.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Jinqing was mild and forbearing. Candidates who came to plead their cases or demand favorable posts might harangue him for thousands of words or raise their voices in fury, yet he always received them with equanimity and never showed irritation.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，拜吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 29 he was appointed vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 前後典選五年，政既寬弛，胥吏多因緣為奸，賄賂大行。

translations.literal: Before and after he presided over selections for five years; since administration was already lenient and lax, clerks often used opportunities to commit wickedness, and bribes flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Over five years in charge of the examinations, his administration grew lax; clerks exploited the slackness for corruption, and bribery became widespread.

sentences.zh: 時天下承平，每年赴選常萬余人。

translations.literal: At the time the realm under Heaven enjoyed peace, and each year those coming for selection regularly exceeded ten thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was at peace, and more than ten thousand candidates presented themselves for examination each year.

sentences.zh: 李林甫為尚書，專任廟堂，銓事唯委晉卿及同列侍郎宋遙主之。

translations.literal: Li Linfu served as Minister, monopolizing temple and court; selection matters were solely entrusted to Jinqing and his colleague Vice Minister Song Yao to manage.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu, as minister of personnel, dominated the court and left the examinations entirely to Jinqing and his fellow vice minister Song Yao.

sentences.zh: 選人既多，每年兼命他官有識者同考定書判，務求其實。

translations.literal: Since candidates were so numerous, each year they also appointed other officials of discernment jointly to examine and fix the written judgments, striving to seek the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Because the candidate pool was so large, each year additional experienced officials were brought in to grade the written examinations as rigorously as possible.

sentences.zh: 天寶二年春，御史中丞張倚男奭參選，晉卿與遙以倚初承恩，欲悅附之，考選人判等凡六十四人，分甲乙丙科，奭在其首。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Tianbao, Censor-in-Chief Zhang Yi's son Shi participated in selection; Jinqing and Yao, because Zhang Yi had just received favor, wished to please and attach themselves to him; they examined the candidates' judgment grades totaling sixty-four persons, divided into jia, yi, and bing categories, with Shi at the head.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Tianbao 2 (743), Zhang Yi's son Shi entered the examinations. Hoping to curry favor with the newly favored Zhang Yi, Jinqing and Yao ranked sixty-four candidates in three tiers—and placed Shi at the top.

sentences.zh: 眾知奭不讀書，論議紛然。

translations.literal: The crowd knew Shi did not read books, and discussions were turbulent.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knew Shi was illiterate, and outrage spread through the capital.

sentences.zh: 有蘇孝慍者，嘗為范陽薊令，事安祿山，具其事告之。

translations.literal: There was one Su Xiaoyin, who had once been Magistrate of Ji in Fanyang, served An Lushan, and fully reported the matter to him.
translations.idiomatic: A former magistrate of Ji in Fanyang named Su Xiaoyin, who was now attached to An Lushan, reported the affair to him in full.

sentences.zh: 祿山恩寵特異，謁見不常，因而奏之。

translations.literal: Lushan enjoyed favor and grace exceptionally special; audiences were not regular, and thus he submitted a memorial about it.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan held extraordinary favor at court and had irregular access to the emperor, through which channel he brought the matter before the throne.

sentences.zh: 玄宗大集登科人，禦花萼樓親試，登第者十無一二；

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong greatly gathered those who had passed the examinations, personally tested them at the Hua'e Pavilion, and those who passed numbered scarcely one or two in ten;
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong summoned the newly passed candidates to the Hua'e Pavilion for a personal examination; fewer than one in ten succeeded.

sentences.zh: 而奭手持試紙，竟日不下一字，時謂之「曳白」。

translations.literal: Yet Shi held the examination paper and for a whole day did not write a single character; at the time he was called "dragging the blank."
translations.idiomatic: Shi held his examination paper and could not write a single character all day long—they called it "dragging a blank sheet."

sentences.zh: 上怒，晉卿貶為安康郡太守，遙為武當郡太守，張倚為淮陽太守。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry; Jinqing was demoted to Governor of Ankang Commandery, Yao to Governor of Wudang Commandery, and Zhang Yi to Governor of Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's wrath fell on them all: Jinqing was banished to prefect of Ankang, Yao to prefect of Wudang, and Zhang Yi to prefect of Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 敕曰：「門庭之間，不能訓子；

translations.literal: An edict said: "Within his own gates he could not instruct his son;
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "He could not discipline his son under his own roof;

sentences.zh: 選調之際，仍以托人。

translations.literal: at the time of selection and assignment, he still entrusted matters to others."
translations.idiomatic: at examination time he still used influence on others' behalf."

sentences.zh: 」時士子皆以為戲笑。

translations.literal: At the time scholar-officials all took it as a jest and laughter.
translations.idiomatic: The literati treated the whole affair as a public laughingstock.

sentences.zh: 天寶三載閏二月，轉魏郡太守，充河北采訪處置使，居職三年，政化洽聞。

translations.literal: In the intercalary second month of the third year of Tianbao he was transferred to Governor of Wei Commandery, concurrently serving as Hebei Investigation and Disposition Commissioner; in office three years, his government and transformation were widely heard of.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary second month of Tianbao 3 (744) he became prefect of Wei and Hebei investigation commissioner; after three years his enlightened rule was renowned throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 會入計，因上表請歸鄉里。

translations.literal: When he came in for the annual accounting, he thereby submitted a memorial requesting to return to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: While in the capital for his annual report to the court, he petitioned to visit his hometown.

sentences.zh: 既至壺關，望縣門而步。

translations.literal: When he had arrived at Huguan, gazing at the county gate he walked on foot.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Huguan he dismounted and walked on foot as he approached the county gate.

sentences.zh: 小吏進曰：「太守位高德重，不宜自輕。

translations.literal: A petty clerk advanced and said: "The governor's position is high and his virtue weighty; he should not slight himself."
translations.idiomatic: A clerk came forward and said, "Your Excellency holds high rank and great prestige—you should not humble yourself."

sentences.zh: 」晉卿曰：「《禮》：『下公門，式路馬。

translations.literal: Jinqing said: "The Rites states: 'When descending from the duke's gate, bow to the road horses.'
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing replied, "The Book of Rites says: 'When leaving the duke's gate, one bows toward the horses on the road.'

sentences.zh: 』況父母之邦，所宜尊敬。

translations.literal: How much more, then, one's parents' homeland—what ought to be respected."
translations.idiomatic: How much more should one show respect in the land of one's parents?"

sentences.zh: 汝何言哉！

translations.literal: What words are you speaking!"
translations.idiomatic: What sort of talk is that!"

sentences.zh: 」大會鄉黨，歡飲累日而去。

translations.literal: He greatly gathered the village kin, drank in joy for many days, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He held a great feast for his kinsmen and neighbors, reveling for days before departing.

sentences.zh: 又俸錢三萬為鄉學本，以教授子弟。

translations.literal: He also set aside thirty thousand in salary cash as capital for the village school, to instruct the young.
translations.idiomatic: He also endowed the local school with thirty thousand cash from his salary to educate the village youth.

sentences.zh: 尋改河東太守、河東采訪使，入為尚書、東京留守，征為憲部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Governor of Hedong and Hedong Investigation Commissioner, entered the capital as Minister and Eastern Capital Intendant, and was summoned as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to prefect of Hedong and Hedong investigation commissioner, then recalled to serve as minister and intendant of the Eastern Capital before being appointed minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 屬祿山叛逆，楊國忠以晉卿有時望，將抑之，乃奏云：「宜以大臣鎮東道。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, Yang Guozhong, because Jinqing had contemporary renown and wished to suppress him, memorialized saying: "A great minister ought to guard the eastern circuit."
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Yang Guozhong, wishing to sideline the popular Jinqing, memorialized that a senior minister should be posted to guard the eastern circuit.

sentences.zh: 」遂出為陜州刺史、陜虢兩州防禦使。

translations.literal: Thus he was sent out as Governor of Shaan Prefecture and Defense Commissioner of the two prefectures of Shaan and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing was accordingly sent out as prefect of Shaan and defense commissioner for Shaan and Guo.

sentences.zh: 及入對，固辭老病，由是忤旨，改憲部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: When he entered for audience he firmly declined on grounds of age and illness; thereby he offended the imperial will and was changed to Minister of Justice with retirement.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience he firmly pleaded age and infirmity, thereby offending the emperor, who reassigned him as retired minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 及朝廷失守，衣冠流離道路，多為逆黨所脅，自陳希烈、張均已下數十人盡赴洛陽，晉卿潛遁山谷，南投金州。

translations.literal: When the court lost its hold, officials in caps and gowns wandered the roads, many coerced by the rebel faction; from Chen Xilie and Zhang Jun downward dozens all went to Luoyang, while Jinqing secretly fled into mountain valleys and went south to Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, court officials fled along the roads, many forced into rebel service; from Chen Xilie and Zhang Jun on down, dozens went over to Luoyang, while Jinqing hid in the mountains and made his way south to Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會肅宗至鳳翔，手詔追晉卿赴行在，即日拜為左相，軍國大務悉以咨之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong reached Fengxiang, by handwritten edict he summoned Jinqing to the mobile court; that same day he was appointed Left Chancellor, and all great affairs of army and state were wholly entrusted to his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong reached Fengxiang he issued a personal summons for Jinqing to join the court; that same day Jinqing was appointed left chancellor, and all major military and civil affairs were referred to him.

sentences.zh: 既收兩京，以功封韓國公，食實封五百戶，改為侍中。

translations.literal: Once the two capitals were recovered, for his merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Han with five hundred households of substantive fief, and was changed to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After the two capitals were recovered he was enfeoffed as Duke of Han with a substantive fief of five hundred households and appointed palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 後以賊寇漸除，屢乞骸骨，優詔許之，罷知政事，為太子太傅。

translations.literal: Later, because the bandit invaders were gradually eliminated, he repeatedly begged to surrender his bones; a gracious edict permitted it, he ceased managing state affairs, and became Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels were gradually suppressed he repeatedly asked to retire; the emperor graciously consented, relieved him of administrative duties, and appointed him grand tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝思舊臣，復拜為侍中。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor thought of old ministers and again appointed him Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor, missing his veteran minister, recalled him as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 晉卿寬厚廉謹，為政舉大綱，不問小過，所到有惠化。

translations.literal: Jinqing was generous, thick, honest, and cautious; in governing he raised the great outline and did not inquire into small faults; wherever he arrived there was benevolent transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing was generous, upright, and prudent in office; he governed by broad principles rather than petty infractions, and wherever he served he left a legacy of benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 魏人思之，為立碑頌德。

translations.literal: The people of Wei remembered him and erected a stele praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wei cherished his memory and erected a stele in praise of his virtue.

sentences.zh: 及秉鈞衡，小心畏慎，未嘗忤人意。

translations.literal: When he held the balance and steelyard, he was careful and fearful in caution and never once went against people's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held the highest offices he was cautious and deferential, never giving offense.

sentences.zh: 性聰敏，達練事體，百司文簿，經目必曉，而修身守位，以智自全，議者比漢之胡廣。

translations.literal: His nature was intelligent and keen; he was thoroughly versed in the substance of affairs; documents of the hundred offices, once passing his eyes, he always understood; yet he cultivated himself and guarded his position, preserving himself by wisdom; commentators compared him to Hu Guang of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and experienced, he grasped the workings of government at a glance; yet he cultivated himself and guarded his position with shrewd self-preservation, and critics compared him to Hu Guang of the Han.

sentences.zh: 玄宗崩，肅宗詔晉卿攝冢宰。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong died, Emperor Suzong ordered Jinqing to act as regent.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong died, Suzong ordered Jinqing to serve as regent.

sentences.zh: 上表固辭曰：「臣聞古者殷高宗在諒闇之中，百官聽於冢宰，更無事跡，但存文字。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial firmly declining, saying: "Your servant has heard that in antiquity, when King Gaozong of Yin was in the dark of mourning, the hundred officials listened to the regent—there are no further traces of events, only written words remain."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial firmly declining: "I have read that in antiquity, when King Gaozong of Yin mourned in seclusion, the hundred officials took orders from the regent—but beyond that record we have only the text, no further details."

sentences.zh: 且一時之事，禮不相沿。

translations.literal: Moreover, it was a matter of one time; rites are not transmitted in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, that was a unique circumstance; ritual precedent does not carry forward unchanged."

sentences.zh: 今殘寇猶虞，日殷萬務，皆緣兵馬屯守討襲，善算良謀，立勝擒敵。

translations.literal: Now remnant bandits still cause concern; daily the myriad affairs press in—all depend on armies and horses garrisoned and deployed for pursuit and assault, good calculation and fine strategy, to achieve victory at once and capture the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Today remnant rebels still threaten us, and a thousand urgent matters press daily upon the throne—all requiring troops in the field, sound strategy, and swift victory over the enemy.

sentences.zh: 陛下若行古之道，居喪不言，蒼生何依，百事皆廢。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty follows the ancient way, dwelling in mourning without speaking, on what will the common people rely? A hundred affairs will all be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty follows the ancient way and observes mourning in silence, to whom will the people turn? Every affair of state will founder.

sentences.zh: 伏讀國家起居註，亦於禮部檢見舊敕，恭惟太宗、高宗、、大行皇帝在位之日，皆有國哀，視事不輟，以為君臨天下，難徇常情。

translations.literal: Your servant has reverently read the national Veritable Records and also in the Ministry of Rites examined old edicts; respectfully considering that during the days when Taizong, Gaozong, and the late emperor held the throne, whenever there was national mourning they did not cease attending to affairs, holding that to rule all under Heaven one cannot follow ordinary sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: I have consulted the court diaries and old edicts preserved in the Ministry of Rites: Taizong, Gaozong, and the late emperor all continued to govern during periods of national mourning, holding that one who rules the realm cannot indulge ordinary grief.

sentences.zh: 今遺詔有處分，皇帝宜三日而聽政。

translations.literal: Now the testamentary edict has provisions: the emperor ought to hear government after three days.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor's testament expressly provides that the new emperor should assume governance after three days.

sentences.zh: 陛下遵太宗故事，則無冢宰；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty follows Taizong's precedent, then there is no regent;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty follows Taizong's precedent, no regent is needed;

sentences.zh: 遵大行皇帝遺詔，便合聽朝。

translations.literal: if Your Majesty follows the late emperor's testamentary edict, then it is fitting to hear court immediately.
translations.idiomatic: if Your Majesty follows the late emperor's testament, you should take the throne at once.

sentences.zh: 萬姓颙颙，不勝大願。

translations.literal: The myriad people look up eagerly, unable to bear their great wish.
translations.idiomatic: The people look to you with eager hope.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下知理國之重，順人心之切，以義斷恩，從宜無改。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully considers that Your Majesty knows the weight of governing the state, complies with the urgency of people's hearts, cuts off affection by righteousness, and follows what is fitting without change.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to recognize the weight of governing the realm, heed the people's urgent need, set duty above private grief, and do what circumstances require.

sentences.zh: 今朝臣一命已上，皆言臣心昏貌朽，加以疾病，事有急速，斷在須臾，凡聖不同，豈合受詔。

translations.literal: Now court ministers of the first rank and above all say that your servant's mind is dim and his appearance decayed, moreover afflicted with illness; affairs have urgent speed, decisions hang in an instant; ordinary and sage are not the same—how could it be fitting to receive the edict?
translations.idiomatic: The ministers of the first rank and above all say my mind is clouded, my body worn out, and my illness severe; urgent affairs cannot wait on a moment's delay. How can an ordinary man accept a mandate meant for a sage?

sentences.zh: 陛下發哀已五日矣，願準遺詔聽政，則四夷萬國，無任悲幸。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has begun mourning for five days already; I wish you would follow the testamentary edict and hear government—then the four barbarians and ten thousand states will be unable to bear their grief and good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has mourned for five days already; I pray you will follow the testament and assume governance—the four quarters and all nations will rejoice amid their sorrow."

sentences.zh: 」肅宗時疾彌留，覽表殞絕，乃許。

translations.literal: Suzong at the time was gravely ill and lingering; reading the memorial he collapsed as if dead, then permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong was then gravely ill; reading the memorial he was overcome with grief, then consented.

sentences.zh: 數日，肅宗晏駕，代宗踐祚，又詔晉卿攝冢宰。

translations.literal: Several days later Suzong passed away; Daizong ascended the throne and again ordered Jinqing to act as regent.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Suzong died and Daizong ascended the throne; he too ordered Jinqing to serve as regent.

sentences.zh: 晉卿上表懇辭曰：「臣以昔者天子居喪之時，百官聽於冢宰者，蓋君幼小，禦極事殷，情理當然。

translations.literal: Jinqing submitted a memorial earnestly declining, saying: "Your servant holds that in former times when the Son of Heaven dwelt in mourning and the hundred officials listened to the regent, it was because the ruler was young and small, and assuming the apex while affairs pressed—reason and feeling made it natural."
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing submitted another earnest refusal: "In former times when the Son of Heaven mourned and officials took orders from a regent, it was because the ruler was a child and affairs were pressing—such an arrangement was only natural."

sentences.zh: 沿革不一，今古異同，而周武、漢文，合於通變，垂範作則，可舉而行。

translations.literal: Continuity and change are not uniform; past and present differ in sameness and difference; yet King Wu of Zhou and Emperor Wen of Han conformed to adapting through change, left models and made standards that can be raised up and practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Customs differ across ages, yet King Wu of Zhou and Emperor Wen of Han adapted wisely to circumstance and left models we may follow.

sentences.zh: 又士或墨缞，時遇金革，豈非銜恤，謂義在斷恩。

translations.literal: Moreover, a gentleman may wear ink mourning garments; when the time meets metal and weapons, is it not holding grief in the breast—meaning that righteousness lies in cutting off affection?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, scholars sometimes wear mourning garb even amid war—not because they feel no grief, but because duty requires setting private sorrow aside.

sentences.zh: 且百善之至，無加於孝也，其有容瘁心絕，指景悼生，此匹夫守節之常情，殊王者嗣續之大計。

translations.literal: Moreover, of the hundred virtues the utmost—none surpasses filial piety; yet there are those whose appearance is haggard and whose heart is severed, who point to the sun and mourn life—this is the ordinary feeling of a common man guarding integrity, quite different from the great plan of a king continuing the succession.
translations.idiomatic: Filial piety is the highest of virtues, yet wasting away in grief and mourning one's own life is the conduct of a private man—not the great concern of a ruler who must secure the succession.

sentences.zh: 昨二十日，陛下於大行皇帝柩前即位，是承先帝遺顧之言，亦前代不易之典。

translations.literal: Yesterday, the twentieth day, Your Majesty ascended the throne before the bier of the late emperor—this carries out the late emperor's parting charge and is also an unchanging canon of former generations.
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth day Your Majesty took the throne before the late emperor's bier—fulfilling his final charge and following an immemorial precedent.

sentences.zh: 則知所略不為害，所存是適權，防威滅端，所利者大。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that what is set aside does no harm, what is preserved is fitting expedience; guarding against peril and extinguishing beginnings—the benefit is great.
translations.idiomatic: What is set aside does no harm; what is preserved serves the greater good—preventing disaster at its root yields the greatest benefit.

sentences.zh: 陛下因心純至，天地明察。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's heart arising from purity reaches utmost; Heaven and Earth see clearly.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's filial heart is pure and sincere—Heaven and Earth witness it.

sentences.zh: 伏以報劬勞之恩，申罔極之思，終身之痛，豈計朝夕！

translations.literal: Your servant considers that repaying toilsome labor's grace and expressing boundless longing—lifelong pain, how could one reckon by morning and evening!
translations.idiomatic: To repay a parent's toil and express boundless grief is a lifelong sorrow—not a matter of days alone!

sentences.zh: 但以一日之內，萬務在中，須達宸聰，始成國政。

translations.literal: Yet within a single day the myriad affairs lie at the center; the imperial ear must be reached before state government can be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Yet within a single day ten thousand affairs demand the emperor's ear—only then can the state be governed.

sentences.zh: 百僚萬姓及僧道耆壽等，相顧聚言，以臣老且無能，愚豈測聖，況久無居攝，臣不敢奉詔。

translations.literal: The hundred officials, myriad people, and monks, Daoists, and elders of long years alike, looking at one another gathered in speech, say that your servant is old and without ability—how could stupidity fathom the sage? Moreover, for long there has been no regency; your servant dares not accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Officials, common people, monks, and elders alike agree that I am old and incompetent—how could a fool measure a sage? Regency has long been obsolete; I dare not accept this charge.

sentences.zh: 特乞陛下遵遺命，三日而政。

translations.literal: I especially beg Your Majesty to follow the testamentary command and govern after three days.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to follow the testament and assume governance after three days.

sentences.zh: 臣博聽眾情，不勝懇願，伏望割痛抑哀，則天下悲幸。

translations.literal: Your servant broadly hears the multitude's feelings and cannot bear his earnest wish; bowing head, I hope you will cut pain and restrain grief—then all under Heaven will grieve and rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: Having heard the people's unanimous plea, I cannot but beg you to set grief aside for the nation's sake—the realm will mourn and rejoice together."

sentences.zh: 」上號泣從之。

translations.literal: The emperor wailed and wept and followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and assented.

sentences.zh: 時晉卿年已衰暮，又患兩足，上特許肩輿至中書，入閣不趨，累日一視事。

translations.literal: At the time Jinqing's years were already declining in old age and he also suffered in both feet; the emperor specially permitted a shoulder litter to the Secretariat, entering the gate without hurrying, attending to affairs once every several days.
translations.idiomatic: By then Jinqing was elderly and afflicted in both legs; the emperor specially allowed him a sedan chair to the Secretariat, exemption from hurrying in court, and attendance at office only every few days.

sentences.zh: 歷三朝，皆以謹密見稱。

translations.literal: Through three reigns he was all praised for cautious secrecy.
translations.idiomatic: Through three reigns he was praised for his discretion and prudence.

sentences.zh: 廣德初，吐蕃寇長安。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangde, the Tibetans raided Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Guangde era (763), the Tibetans invaded Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 晉卿時病臥於私第，蕃聞之，輿入逼脅，晉卿閉口不言，賊不敢害。

translations.literal: Jinqing at the time lay ill in his private residence; the Tibetans heard of it, entered by litter to coerce him, but Jinqing closed his mouth and did not speak—the bandits did not dare harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing lay ill at home; the Tibetans heard of him and came in a litter to coerce him, but he remained silent and they did not dare harm him.

sentences.zh: 及上自陜至，冊為太保，罷知政事，又詔以太保致仕。

translations.literal: When the emperor came from Shaan, Jinqing was enfeoffed as Grand Mentor, ceased managing state affairs, and was again ordered to retire as Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from Shaan, Jinqing was appointed grand mentor, relieved of administrative duties, and granted retirement in that rank.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年四月薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Yongtai he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month of Yongtai 1 (765).

sentences.zh: 輟朝三日，令京兆少尹一員護喪事，緣葬諸物並官給，賻絹布五百段、米粟五百石。

translations.literal: Court mourning was suspended for three days; one Junior Intendant of the Capital District was ordered to oversee funeral affairs; all items connected with burial were supplied by the government; condolence gifts of five hundred bolts of silk cloth and five hundred piculs of grain and millet.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourning was observed for three days; a junior intendant of the capital was assigned to oversee the funeral; all burial expenses were provided by the state, with five hundred bolts of silk and five hundred piculs of grain as condolence gifts.

sentences.zh: 太常議謚曰「懿獻」。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices deliberated on the posthumous name "Yi Xian."
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices proposed the posthumous name Yi Xian ("Benevolent and Offering").

sentences.zh: 初，晉卿東都留守，引用大理評事元載為推官。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jinqing was Intendant of the Eastern Capital, he employed Yuan Zai, Reviewing Official of the Court of Judicial Review, as investigating officer.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Jinqing served as intendant of the Eastern Capital, he appointed Yuan Zai of the Court of Judicial Review as his investigating officer.

sentences.zh: 至是載為中書侍郎、平章事，懷舊恩，諷有司改謚曰文貞。

translations.literal: By this time Zai was Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Co-Equal to the Department of State Affairs; cherishing old grace, he hinted to the responsible offices to change the posthumous name to Wen Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yuan Zai was vice minister of the Secretariat and chief councilor; remembering old favors, he persuaded the authorities to change the posthumous name to Wen Zhen ("Cultured and Upright").

sentences.zh: 大歷七年，令配享肅宗廟庭。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dali he was ordered to share sacrifice in Suzong's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 7 (772) he was granted posthumous worship in Suzong's ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: =裴冕=裴冕，河東人也，為河東冠族。

translations.literal: = Pei Mian = Pei Mian was a man of Hedong and ranked among Hedong's foremost clans.
translations.idiomatic: — Pei Mian — Pei Mian was a native of Hedong and belonged to one of the region's leading families.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，以門廕再遷渭南縣尉，以吏道聞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, through hereditary privilege he was twice transferred to Sheriff of Weinan County and became known for the way of officials.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao era he entered service by hereditary privilege and rose to sheriff of Weinan, gaining a reputation for administrative competence.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞王鉷充京畿采訪使，表為判官。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wang Hong, serving as Metropolitan Investigation Commissioner, recommended him as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor-in-Chief Wang Hong served as metropolitan investigation commissioner, he recommended Mian as his administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 遷監察御史，歷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Investigating Censor and successively served as Attending Censor in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to investigating censor and then served as palace attending censor.

sentences.zh: 冕雖無學術，守職通明，果於臨事，鉷甚委之。

translations.literal: Although Mian had no learning or arts, he guarded his office with clear understanding, was resolute in facing affairs, and Hong greatly entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Though lacking scholarly training, Mian was clear-minded in office and decisive in action; Wang Hong relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 及鉷得罪伏法，時宰臣李林甫方竊權柄，人鹹懼之，鉷賓佐數百，不敢窺鉷門。

translations.literal: When Hong was guilty and executed by law, at the time Chief Minister Li Linfu was just usurping power; people all feared him; Hong's guest aides numbered in the hundreds and did not dare peek at Hong's gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Hong was executed, Li Linfu held power and everyone feared him; none of Hong's hundreds of retainers dared approach his house.

sentences.zh: 冕獨收鉷屍，親自護喪，瘞於近郊，冕自是知名。

translations.literal: Mian alone collected Hong's corpse, personally escorted the funeral, and buried him in the near suburbs; from this Mian became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Mian alone recovered Hong's body, personally conducted the funeral, and buried him in the suburbs—thereby winning widespread renown.

sentences.zh: 河西節度使哥舒翰表為行軍司馬，累遷員外郎中。

translations.literal: Geshu Han, Military Commissioner of Hexi, recommended him as campaigning marshal and he was repeatedly transferred to Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Geshu Han, military commissioner of Hexi, recommended him as campaigning marshal, and he rose to vice director.

sentences.zh: 玄宗幸蜀，至益昌郡，遙詔太子充天下兵馬元帥，以冕為御史中丞兼左庶子，為之副。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong went to Shu; reaching Yichang Commandery, from afar he edicted the Heir Apparent to serve as Commander-in-Chief of all armies and horses under Heaven, appointing Mian Censor-in-Chief concurrently as Left Subordinate to the Heir Apparent as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong fled to Shu and reached Yichang, he issued a distant edict appointing the crown prince commander of all armies under heaven, with Mian as censor-in-chief and left subordinate to the heir as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 是時，冕為河西行軍司馬，授御史中丞，詔赴朝廷。

translations.literal: At this time Mian was campaigning marshal of Hexi; he was granted Censor-in-Chief and ordered to proceed to court.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Mian was campaigning marshal in Hexi; he received appointment as censor-in-chief and was ordered to the court.

sentences.zh: 遇太子於平涼，具陳事勢，勸之朔方，亟入靈武。

translations.literal: He met the Heir Apparent at Pingliang, fully stated the situation, urged him toward Shuofang, and urgently to enter Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: He met the crown prince at Pingliang, laid out the full situation, and urged him to proceed to Shuofang and enter Lingwu without delay.

sentences.zh: 冕與杜鴻漸、崔漪等勸進曰：「主上厭勤大位，南幸蜀川，宗社神器，須有所歸，天意人事，不可固違。

translations.literal: Mian with Du Hongjian, Cui Yi, and others urged advancement, saying: "The sovereign has grown weary of toiling in the great position and gone south to favor Shu; the altars of state and the sacred vessel must have someone to return to them—Heaven's intent and human affairs cannot be stubbornly violated."
translations.idiomatic: Mian, together with Du Hongjian, Cui Yi, and others, urged the prince to ascend the throne: "The emperor has grown weary of rule and fled south to Shu; the altars of state and the imperial regalia must find a home—Heaven's will and human necessity cannot be defied."

sentences.zh: 若逡巡退讓，失億兆心，則大事去矣！

translations.literal: If you hesitate and yield in retreat, losing the hearts of the hundred millions, then the great enterprise will be lost!
translations.idiomatic: If you hesitate and step aside, losing the hearts of the people, the cause will be lost!

sentences.zh: 臣等猶知之，況賢智乎！

translations.literal: We your ministers still understand this—how much more so one of talent and wisdom!
translations.idiomatic: Even we ministers understand this—how much more so a man of your wisdom!

sentences.zh: 」太子曰：「南平寇逆，奉迎鑾輿，退居儲貳，侍膳左右，豈不樂哉！

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent said: "When the south is pacified and rebels subdued, when we welcome back the imperial carriage, retire to the position of heir, and attend at meals left and right—is that not joy itself!"
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince replied: "When the south is pacified and rebels crushed, when we escort the emperor home and I resume my place as heir, attending at his side—is that not happiness enough?"

sentences.zh: 公等何言之過也？

translations.literal: Why do you gentlemen speak so excessively?
translations.idiomatic: Why do you speak so extravagantly?

sentences.zh: 」冕與杜鴻漸又進曰：「殿下藉累聖之資，有天下之表。

translations.literal: Mian and Du Hongjian again advanced, saying: "Your Highness, relying on the accumulated virtue of successive sages, possesses the outward bearing to rule all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Mian and Du Hongjian pressed further: "Your Highness inherits the accumulated virtue of past emperors and bears the bearing of one meant to rule the realm.

sentences.zh: 元貞萬國，二十余年，殷憂啟聖，正在今日。

translations.literal: The throne's steadfast virtue has held myriad states for more than twenty years; deep sorrow giving birth to sagacity—right today is the time.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty has stood firm for more than twenty years; it is today's deep crisis that summons forth a true ruler.

sentences.zh: 所從殿下六軍將士，皆關輔百姓，日夜思歸。

translations.literal: The six-army officers and soldiers who follow Your Highness are all common people of the Guanzhong region, day and night thinking of returning home.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and soldiers who follow you are common folk from the Guanzhong heartland, longing night and day to return home.

sentences.zh: 大軍一散，不可復集，不如因而撫之以從眾，臣等敢以死請。

translations.literal: Once the great army disperses, it cannot be gathered again; it is better to take advantage of this and reassure them to follow the multitude—we dare request this even at the cost of our lives.
translations.idiomatic: Once this army disperses, it cannot be reassembled; better to seize the moment, reassure the troops, and follow the people's will—we beg this even at the price of our lives.

sentences.zh: 」凡勸進五上，乃依。

translations.literal: In all they urged advancement five times before he complied.
translations.idiomatic: After five rounds of urging, he finally assented.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，以定策功，遷中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，倚以為政。

translations.literal: When Suzong ascended the throne, for his merit in settling the strategy he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Secretariat, Associate Chancellor, and relied upon in governing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong took the throne, Mian was promoted to vice minister of the secretariat and associate chancellor for his role in the succession and was entrusted with governing.

sentences.zh: 冕性忠勤，悉心奉公，稍得人心。

translations.literal: Mian by nature was loyal and diligent, devoting his heart to public service, and gradually won people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was loyal and diligent by nature, devoted himself wholeheartedly to public service, and gradually won people's trust.

sentences.zh: 然不識大體，以聚人曰財，乃下令賣官鬻爵，度尼僧道士，以儲積為務。

translations.literal: Yet he did not grasp the larger picture; holding that gathering people is called wealth, he then ordered the sale of offices and ranks, ordaining Buddhist nuns, monks, and Daoist priests, making accumulation his chief task.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he failed to see the bigger picture; believing that amassing people was wealth, he ordered the sale of offices and titles, ordained nuns, monks, and Daoist priests, and made hoarding his main priority.

sentences.zh: 人不願者，科令就之，其價益賤，事轉為弊。

translations.literal: Those who did not wish it were compelled by statute to comply; the prices grew ever cheaper, and the affair turned increasingly harmful.
translations.idiomatic: Those who refused were forced by regulation to comply anyway; prices kept falling, and the practice grew ever more corrupt.

sentences.zh: 肅宗移幸鳳翔，罷冕知政事，遷右僕射。

translations.literal: When Suzong moved his court to Fengxiang, Mian was removed from managing affairs of state and transferred to Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong relocated to Fengxiang, Mian was removed from the chancellorship and made right vice director.

sentences.zh: 兩京平，以功封冀國公，食實封五百戶。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were pacified, for his merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji with five hundred households of actual fief.
translations.idiomatic: After the two capitals were recovered, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji with five hundred taxable households for his service.

sentences.zh: 尋加御史大夫、成都尹，充劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: Soon additionally Grand Censor, Intendant of Chengdu, serving as Military Commissioner of Jiannan West.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made grand censor and intendant of Chengdu, serving as military commissioner of Jiannan West.

sentences.zh: 又入為右僕射。

translations.literal: He again entered court as Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned to court as right vice director.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，與裴遵慶等並集賢待制。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, together with Pei Zunqing and others he was made Attendant Drafting Official at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai 1 (765), he and Pei Zunqing and others were appointed attendant drafting officials at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 代宗求舊，拜冕兼御史大夫，充護山陵使。

translations.literal: Daizong seeking old associates, appointed Mian concurrently Grand Censor, charged as Commissioner for Guarding the Imperial Tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking out old associates, Emperor Daizong appointed Mian concurrently grand censor and commissioner for guarding the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 冕以幸臣李輔國權盛，將附之，乃表輔國親昵術士中書舍人劉烜充山陵使判官。

translations.literal: Mian, because favored minister Li Fuguo's power was ascendant and intending to attach himself to him, memorialized that Liu Xuan, Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat and an occultist intimate with Fuguo, serve as adjudicator for the tomb commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: As the favored minister Li Fuguo's power rose, Mian sought to align with him and recommended Liu Xuan, a drafting secretary and occultist close to Fuguo, as adjudicator on the tomb commission.

sentences.zh: 烜坐法，冕坐貶施州刺史。

translations.literal: Xuan was punished under the law; Mian was demoted to Prefect of Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan was punished for breaking the law, and Mian was demoted to prefect of Shi.

sentences.zh: 數月，移澧州刺史，復征為左僕射。

translations.literal: After several months he was transferred to Prefect of Li, then again summoned as Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was transferred to prefect of Li, then recalled as left vice director.

sentences.zh: 元載秉政。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai held the reins of government.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai held power.

sentences.zh: 載為新平縣尉，王鉷辟在巡內，冕常引之，載頗德冕。

translations.literal: When Zai was magistrate of Xinping County, Wang Hong recruited him within his circuit; Mian often recommended him, and Zai was quite grateful to Mian.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zai had been magistrate of Xinping County, Wang Hong recruited him into his circuit staff; Mian had often recommended him, and Zai felt deep gratitude toward Mian.

sentences.zh: 會宰臣杜鴻漸卒，載遂舉冕代之。

translations.literal: When chief minister Du Hongjian died, Zai then recommended Mian to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When chief minister Du Hongjian died, Yuan Zai recommended Mian to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 冕時已衰瘵，載以其順己，引為同列。

translations.literal: Mian was by then weakened by illness; Zai, because he complied with him, brought him in as colleague on the council.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was by then frail and ill; Yuan Zai, finding him compliant, brought him onto the council as a colleague.

sentences.zh: 受命之際，蹈舞絕倒，載趨而扶起，代為謝詞。

translations.literal: At the moment of receiving the appointment, he danced with joy and fell flat; Zai rushed forward to help him up and spoke thanks on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When he received the appointment, he danced for joy and collapsed; Yuan Zai rushed to help him up and delivered the thanks on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 冕兼掌兵權留守之任，俸錢每月二千余貫。

translations.literal: Mian concurrently held military authority and the duties of capital intendant; his salary was more than two thousand strings per month.
translations.idiomatic: Mian also held military authority and the duties of capital intendant, with a monthly salary of more than two thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 性本侈靡，好尚車服及營珍饌，名馬在櫪，直數百金者常十數。

translations.literal: By nature he was extravagant, fond of carriages and dress and preparing rare delicacies; famed horses in the stable worth several hundred gold pieces numbered regularly more than ten.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was extravagant, fond of fine carriages and dress and of preparing rare delicacies; he kept more than ten famed horses in his stables, each worth several hundred gold pieces.

sentences.zh: 每會賓友，滋味品數，坐客有昧於名者。

translations.literal: Whenever he gathered guests, the flavors and variety of dishes were such that seated guests could not name some of them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he entertained guests, the dishes were so numerous and exotic that some seated guests could not even name what they were eating.

sentences.zh: 自創巾子，其狀新奇，市肆因而效之，呼為「僕射樣」。

translations.literal: He devised his own headcloth; its form was novel, and market shops copied it, calling it the "Vice Director style."
translations.idiomatic: He designed his own style of headcloth; its shape was so novel that shops copied it, calling it the "Vice Director style."

sentences.zh: 初代鴻漸，小吏以俸錢文簿白之，冕顧子弟，喜見於色，其嗜利若此。

translations.literal: When he first replaced Hongjian, a petty clerk reported the salary ledger to him; Mian looked toward his sons and nephews, delight showing in his expression—such was his craving for profit.
translations.idiomatic: When he first replaced Du Hongjian, a clerk presented him with the salary ledger; Mian glanced at his sons and nephews with visible delight—such was his greed.

sentences.zh: 拜職未盈月，卒，大歷四年十二月也。

translations.literal: Less than a full month after taking office he died—in the twelfth month of the fourth year of Dali.
translations.idiomatic: Less than a month after taking office he died, in the twelfth month of Dali 4 (769).

sentences.zh: 上悼之，輟朝三日，贈太尉，賻制五百匹、粟五百石。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned him, suspended court for three days, posthumously appointed him Grand Preceptor, and granted condolence gifts of five hundred bolts and five hundred piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him, suspended court for three days, posthumously appointed him grand preceptor, and granted five hundred bolts of silk and five hundred piculs of grain as condolence gifts.

sentences.zh: =裴遵慶=裴遵慶，絳州聞喜人也。

translations.literal: = Pei Zunqing = Pei Zunqing was a native of Wenxi in Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: — Pei Zunqing — Pei Zunqing was a native of Wenxi in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 代襲冠冕，為河東著族。

translations.literal: For generations they inherited rank and distinction, a prominent clan of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family had held rank and distinction, and they were a prominent clan of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 遵慶志氣深厚，機鑒敏達，自幼強學，博涉載籍，謹身晦跡，不幹當世之務。

translations.literal: Zunqing's will was deep and firm, his insight sharp and penetrating; from youth he studied strenuously, broadly traversing the written records, keeping himself disciplined and concealing his tracks, not meddling in affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing had a deep and steadfast character and keen, penetrating judgment; from youth he studied hard, read widely in the classics, kept himself disciplined and out of sight, and did not meddle in the affairs of the day.

sentences.zh: 以門廕累授潞府司法參軍，時年已老，未為人所知。

translations.literal: Through hereditary privilege he cumulatively received appointment as Legal Administrator in Lu Prefecture; by then he was already old and not known to others.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he rose cumulatively to legal administrator in Lu Prefecture; by then he was already elderly and little known.

sentences.zh: 隨調吏部，授大理寺丞，剖斷刑獄，舉正綱條，理行始著。

translations.literal: Following regular reassignment to the Ministry of Personnel, he was appointed Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review; in adjudicating criminal cases and upholding statutes, his governing conduct first became notable.
translations.idiomatic: On routine reassignment to the Ministry of Personnel, he was appointed assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review; in adjudicating criminal cases and upholding the law, his administrative ability first became evident.

sentences.zh: 遷司門員外、吏部員外郎，專判南曹。

translations.literal: Promoted to Vice Director of the Gate Office and Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel, exclusively deciding Southern Bureau cases.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Gate Office and vice director in the Ministry of Personnel, with sole charge of the Southern Bureau.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，海內無事，九流輻輳會府，每歲吏部選人，動盈萬數。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, all within the seas was at peace; the nine streams of talent crowded the capital, and each year Ministry of Personnel candidates regularly exceeded ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era the realm was at peace; men of every calling thronged the capital, and each year the Ministry of Personnel's candidates regularly numbered more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 遵慶敏識強記，精核文簿，詳而不滯，時稱吏事第一，由是大知名。

translations.literal: Zunqing had keen recognition and strong memory, examining documents with precision, thorough yet unfettered; at the time he was called first in clerical affairs, and by this gained great renown.
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing had a sharp mind and prodigious memory; he scrutinized documents with precision, thorough yet never bogged down, and was acclaimed the finest administrator of his day—by which he gained great renown.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，楊國忠當國，出不附己者例為外官，遵慶亦出為郡守。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao, Yang Guozhong controlled the state; those not attached to him were routinely made outer officials; Zunqing too was sent out as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Tianbao, Yang Guozhong dominated the government and routinely posted those who did not support him to provincial offices; Zunqing was likewise sent out as a prefect.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，征拜給事中、尚書右丞、吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Suzong ascended the throne, he was summoned and appointed Drafting Counselor, Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs (right), and Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong took the throne, Zunqing was summoned and appointed drafting counselor, vice director of the Department of State Affairs, and vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 恭儉克己，遲重謹密，頗有時望。

translations.literal: Respectful and frugal, restraining himself, deliberate and careful—he enjoyed considerable repute in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Respectful and frugal, self-restrained, deliberate and discreet, he enjoyed considerable standing in his day.

sentences.zh: 上元中，蕭華輔政，素知遵慶，每奏見，累稱之，遷黃門侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era, Xiao Hua assisted in government, having long known Zunqing; each time he saw the emperor in memorial audience he repeatedly praised him; Zunqing was promoted to Vice Minister of the Secretariat (Huangmen) and Associate Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shangyuan era, Xiao Hua served as chief minister and, having long known Zunqing, praised him repeatedly at imperial audiences; Zunqing was promoted to vice minister of the secretariat and associate chancellor.

sentences.zh: 廣德初，仆固懷恩阻兵汾上，指中官為詞，上以遵慶忠純，特遣往汾州宣慰懷恩。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangde, Pugu Huai'en blocked the army at Fen; using the eunuchs as pretext, the emperor because Zunqing was loyal and pure specially dispatched him to Fen Prefecture to announce consolation to Huai'en.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Guangde, Pugu Huai'en held his army at Fen and used the eunuchs as a pretext for rebellion; the emperor, trusting Zunqing's loyalty and integrity, specially dispatched him to Fen Prefecture to announce consolation to Huai'en.

sentences.zh: 遵慶既見懷恩，具陳朝旨，懷恩引過聽命，將隨遵慶朝謁，為副將範誌誠以邪說惑之，懷恩遂以懼死為詞。

translations.literal: Once Zunqing had seen Huai'en, he fully stated the court's intent; Huai'en admitted fault and obeyed, about to follow Zunqing to court audience, but deputy general Fan Zhicheng swayed him with perverse talk, and Huai'en then pleaded fear of death.
translations.idiomatic: When Zunqing met Huai'en, he fully conveyed the court's intent; Huai'en admitted his fault and agreed to obey, and was about to follow Zunqing to court, but his deputy Fan Zhicheng swayed him with perverse counsel, and Huai'en then pleaded that he feared for his life.

sentences.zh: 會蕃寇陷京師，乘輿幸陜，遵慶自汾州奔赴行在。

translations.literal: When Tibetan raiders seized the capital and the imperial carriage favored Shan, Zunqing rushed from Fen Prefecture to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetan raiders took the capital and the emperor fled to Shan, Zunqing rushed from Fen Prefecture to join the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 及乘輿還京，以遵慶為太子少傅。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, Zunqing was made Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, Zunqing was appointed junior mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，與裴冕等並於集賢院待制，罷知政事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, together with Pei Mian and others he served as Attendant Drafting Official at the Hall of Assembled Worthies and was removed from managing affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai 1 (765), he and Pei Mian and others were appointed attendant drafting officials at the Hall of Assembled Worthies and removed from the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 尋改吏部尚書、右僕射，復知選事。

translations.literal: Soon changed to Minister of Personnel, Right Vice Director, again managing selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made minister of personnel and right vice director, again in charge of official selection.

sentences.zh: 時選人天興縣尉陳琯於銓庭言詞不遜，淩突無禮，代宗詔付遵慶於省門鞭三十，貶為吉州員外司戶參軍。

translations.literal: At the time the candidate Chen Guan, magistrate of Tianxing County, spoke impertinently at the selection courtyard, insulting and acting without propriety; Daizong edicted that he be handed to Zunqing for thirty lashes at the ministry gate and demoted to Outer Assistant Registrar for Revenue in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a candidate, Chen Guan, magistrate of Tianxing County, spoke insolently at the selection courtyard and behaved with gross disrespect; Emperor Daizong ordered Zunqing to have him flogged thirty times at the ministry gate and demoted him to outer assistant registrar for revenue in Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遵慶敦守儒行，老而彌謹。

translations.literal: Zunqing steadfastly upheld Confucian conduct, growing ever more careful in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing steadfastly upheld Confucian conduct and grew ever more careful in old age.

sentences.zh: 嘗為風狂族侄撾登聞鼓告以不順，上知遵度，不省，其見信如此。

translations.literal: On one occasion a mad cousin by the clan beat the drum at the Hall for Hearing Grievances accusing him of disloyalty; the emperor, knowing Zunqing, did not investigate—the degree of trust was such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Once a deranged clansman beat the drum at the Hall for Hearing Grievances accusing Zunqing of disloyalty; the emperor, knowing Zunqing well, did not even look into it—such was the trust placed in him.

sentences.zh: 大歷十年十月薨於位，年九十余。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the tenth year of Dali he died in office at over ninety years of age.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Dali 10 (775) he died in office at over ninety years of age.

sentences.zh: 遵慶初登省郎，嘗著《王政記》，述今古禮體，識者覽之，知有公輔之量。

translations.literal: When Zunqing first rose to provincial bureau secretary, he once authored "Record of Royal Governance," narrating ancient and modern ritual forms; those who read it knew he had the capacity of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Zunqing first rose to a provincial bureau secretaryship, he wrote the Record of Royal Governance, setting out ancient and modern ritual forms; readers who saw it knew he had the makings of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 遵慶子 向子向，字傃仁，少以門廕歷官至太子司議郎。

translations.literal: Zunqing's son Xiang, Pei Xiang, styled Suren—from youth through hereditary privilege he cumulatively reached the office of Secretariat Drafter of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xiang, styled Suren, was the son of Pei Zunqing; from youth through hereditary privilege he rose cumulatively to secretariat drafter of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 建中初，李紓為同州刺史，奏向為從事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, Li Shu was prefect of Tong Prefecture and memorialized Xiang as his staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianzhong era, Li Shu was prefect of Tong Prefecture and recommended Xiang as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 硃泚反，李懷光又叛河中，使其將趙貴先築壘於同州，紓來奔奉天，向領州務。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci rebelled; Li Huai'guang also rebelled in Hezhong, sending his general Zhao Guixian to build fortifications at Tong Prefecture; Shu fled to Fengtian, and Xiang took charge of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci rebelled, and Li Huai'guang also rebelled in Hezhong, sending his general Zhao Guixian to build fortifications at Tong Prefecture; Li Shu fled to Fengtian, and Xiang took charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貴先因脅縣尉林寶役徒板築，不及期，將斬之，吏人百姓奔竄。

translations.literal: Guixian then coerced the county magistrate Lin Bao to impress laborers for wall-building; when they missed the deadline he was about to execute Lin, and officials and common people fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Guixian then forced the county magistrate Lin Bao to impress laborers for wall-building; when the work fell behind schedule he was about to execute Lin, and officials and commoners fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 向即詣貴先軍壘，以逆順之理責之，貴先感悟，遂來降，故同州不陷。

translations.literal: Xiang immediately went to Guixian's camp and rebuked him with the logic of loyalty versus rebellion; Guixian was moved to understanding, then came over in surrender, and so Tong Prefecture did not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang went at once to Guixian's camp and rebuked him on the grounds of loyalty and rebellion; Guixian was moved and surrendered, and so Tong Prefecture was spared.

sentences.zh: 向由是知名。

translations.literal: From this Xiang became known.
translations.idiomatic: From this Xiang gained renown.

sentences.zh: 累為京兆府戶曹，轉櫟陽、渭南縣令，奏課皆第一，朝廷亟聞其理行，擢為戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: He cumulatively served as Revenue Section Chief in the Capital Metropolitan Prefecture, then as magistrate of Liyang and Weinan; his evaluation reports were all ranked first, the court quickly heard of his governing conduct, and he was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served cumulatively as revenue section chief in the capital metropolitan prefecture, then as magistrate of Liyang and Weinan; his performance reports were always ranked first, the court soon heard of his governance, and he was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 德宗季年，天下方鎮副倅多自選於朝，防一日有變，遂就而授之節制。

translations.literal: In Dezong's later years, many deputies of military commissioners throughout the realm were selected at court lest something happen suddenly—then they could immediately be granted command.
translations.idiomatic: In the late years of Emperor Dezong's reign, many deputies of military commissioners were selected at court so that, should crisis arise, they could immediately be granted full command.

sentences.zh: 向已選為太原少尹，德宗召見喻旨，尋用為行軍司馬、兼御史中丞，改汾州刺史，轉鄭州。

translations.literal: Xiang had already been selected as Junior Intendant of Taiyuan; Dezong summoned him, explained his intent, and soon employed him as campaigning marshal, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, then changed to Prefect of Fen, transferred to Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang had already been selected as junior intendant of Taiyuan; Dezong summoned him, explained his intent, and soon appointed him campaigning marshal and concurrently censor-in-chief, then prefect of Fen, and later transferred him to Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又復為太原少尹，兼河東節度副使。

translations.literal: Again Junior Intendant of Taiyuan, concurrently deputy military commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as junior intendant of Taiyuan, concurrently deputy military commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 改晉州刺史，充本州防禦使，遷虢州刺史。

translations.literal: Changed to Prefect of Jin, serving as defense commissioner of that prefecture, promoted to Prefect of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Jin and defense commissioner of that prefecture, then promoted to prefect of Guo.

sentences.zh: 入為京兆少尹，拜同州刺史，充本州防禦使。

translations.literal: Entered as Junior Intendant of the Capital Metropolitan Prefecture, appointed Prefect of Tong, serving as defense commissioner of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as junior intendant of the capital metropolitan prefecture, was appointed prefect of Tong, and served as defense commissioner of that prefecture.

sentences.zh: 入為大理寺卿，出遷陜虢都防禦、觀察使。

translations.literal: Entered as Director of the Court of Judicial Review; went out promoted to Defense and Observation Commissioner of Shan-Guo circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as director of the Court of Judicial Review, then went out as defense and observation commissioner of the Shan-Guo circuit.

sentences.zh: 三歲，拜左散騎常侍，自常侍復為大理。

translations.literal: After three years, appointed Left Regular Attendant; from Regular Attendant he again became Director of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he was appointed left regular attendant; from that post he again became director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 向本以名相子，以學行自飭，謹守其門風。

translations.literal: Xiang was originally the son of a renowned chief minister; by learning and conduct he restrained himself, carefully preserving his family's ethos.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was the son of a famous chief minister; through learning and conduct he disciplined himself and carefully preserved his family's reputation.

sentences.zh: 歷官仁智推愛，利及於人。

translations.literal: In successive offices he pushed benevolence and wisdom, benefit reaching the people.
translations.idiomatic: In successive offices he extended benevolence and wisdom, bringing benefit to the people.

sentences.zh: 至是，以年過致政，朝廷優異，乃以吏部尚書致仕於新昌裏第。

translations.literal: At this point, because of advanced age he retired from office; the court treated him with exceptional honor, granting retirement as Minister of Personnel at his estate in Xinchang Lane.
translations.idiomatic: At this point, having reached advanced age, he retired; the court treated him with exceptional honor and granted him retirement as minister of personnel at his estate in Xinchang Lane.

sentences.zh: 內外支屬百余人，向所得俸祿，必同其費，及領外任，亦挈而隨之。

translations.literal: More than a hundred internal and external dependents—whatever salary Xiang received he always shared the expenses, and when he took outer appointments he brought them along.
translations.idiomatic: He had more than a hundred dependents within and outside the clan; whatever salary Xiang received he always shared with them, and when he took provincial appointments he brought them along.

sentences.zh: 有孤煢疾苦不能自恤，向尤周給，至今稱其孝睦焉。

translations.literal: Those who were orphaned, alone, ill, or in hardship and could not care for themselves—Xiang especially provided for them roundly; to this day they praise his filial harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Those who were orphaned, alone, sick, or destitute and could not care for themselves he especially supported; to this day he is praised for his filial devotion and familial kindness.

sentences.zh: 大和四年九月卒，年八十。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Taihe he died at age eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of Taihe 4 (830) at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed junior mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 向子 寅子寅，登進士第，累官至御史大夫卒。

translations.literal: Xiang's son Yin, Pei Yin, passed the jinshi examination and cumulatively reached Grand Censor, in which office he died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's son Pei Yin passed the jinshi examination, rose cumulatively to grand censor, and died in that office.

sentences.zh: 寅子 樞子樞，字紀聖，咸通十二年登進士第。

translations.literal: Yin's son Shu, Pei Shu, styled Jisheng, passed the jinshi examination in the twelfth year of Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's son Pei Shu, styled Jisheng, passed the jinshi examination in Xiantong 12 (871).

sentences.zh: 宰相杜審權出鎮河中，辟為從事，得秘書省校書郎，再遷藍田尉。

translations.literal: When chief minister Du Shenquan went out to command Hezhong, he recruited Shu as staff officer; Shu obtained the post of Collator in the Secretariat, then was twice promoted to magistrate of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: When chief minister Du Shenquan went out to command Hezhong, he recruited Shu as a staff officer; Shu obtained the post of collator in the Secretariat and was soon promoted to magistrate of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 直弘文館。

translations.literal: Served on duty at the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He served on duty at the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 大學士王鐸深知之，鐸罷相失職，樞亦久之不調。

translations.literal: Grand Academician Wang Duo deeply appreciated him; when Duo was removed from the chancellorship and lost his position, Shu also went long without reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Academician Wang Duo thought highly of him; when Duo lost the chancellorship and fell from power, Shu also went long without a new appointment.

sentences.zh: 從僖宗幸蜀，中丞李煥奏為殿中侍御史，遷起居郎。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Xizong to Shu, Censor-in-Chief Li Huan memorialized him as Palace Censor; promoted to Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Xizong to Shu, Censor-in-Chief Li Huan recommended him as palace censor; he was later promoted to diarist.

sentences.zh: 中和初，王鐸復見用，以舊恩徙為鄭滑掌書記、檢校司封郎中，賜金紫，入朝歷兵、吏二員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhonghe, Wang Duo was again employed; out of old favor Shu was transferred to Chief Clerk of Zheng-Hua, Acting Director of the Bureau of Enfeoffments, granted gold and purple; entering court he successively served as Vice Director in the Ministries of War and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhonghe, Wang Duo was again employed; out of old favor Shu was transferred to chief clerk of Zheng-Hua and acting director of the Bureau of Enfeoffments, granted gold and purple insignia; returning to court he served successively as vice director in the ministries of war and personnel.

sentences.zh: 龍紀初，擢拜給事中，改京兆尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longji, promoted to Drafting Counselor, changed to Intendant of the Capital Metropolitan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Longji he was promoted to drafting counselor and made intendant of the capital metropolitan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宰相孔緯尤深獎遇。

translations.literal: Chief minister Kong Wei especially deeply praised and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Kong Wei especially favored and promoted him.

sentences.zh: 大順中，緯以用兵無功貶官，樞坐累為右庶子，尋出為歙州刺史。

translations.literal: In Dazhun, Wei was demoted for military failure without achievement; Shu was implicated and made Right Subordinate to the Heir Apparent; soon sent out as Prefect of She.
translations.idiomatic: During Dazhun, Kong Wei was demoted for military failure; Shu was implicated and made right subordinate to the heir apparent, then soon sent out as prefect of She.

sentences.zh: 乾寧初，入為右散騎常侍，從昭宗幸華州，為汴州宣諭使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianning, entered as Right Regular Attendant; following Emperor Zhaozong to Hua Prefecture, served as Envoy to Announce and Console at Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Qianning he entered court as right regular attendant; following Emperor Zhaozong to Hua Prefecture, he served as envoy to announce and console at Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，樞自歙州罷郡歸朝，路經大梁，時硃全忠兵威已振，樞以兄事之，全忠由是重之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shu left his prefecture at She and returned to court, passing through Daliang, at that time Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already ascendant; Shu treated him as an elder brother, and Quanzhong therefore held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shu left his post at She and returned to court, he passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already on the rise, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to hold him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 及樞傳詔，全忠皆稟朝旨，獻奉相繼，昭宗甚悅，遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Shu transmitted edicts, Quanzhong all followed court intent and successive tribute offerings followed; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted him to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu transmitted imperial edicts, Quanzhong followed the court's intent and sent tribute in succession; Emperor Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 時崔胤專政，亦倚全忠，二人因是相結，改樞吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the time Cui Yin monopolized government and also relied on Quanzhong; the two thus allied, and Shu was changed to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Cui Yin dominated the government and also relied on Quanzhong; the two allied through this connection, and Shu was made vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 未幾，換戶部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Before long, exchanged to Vice Minister of Revenue, Associate Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made vice minister of revenue and associate chancellor.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，昭宗幸華州，崔胤貶官，樞亦為工部尚書。

translations.literal: That winter Zhaozong favored Hua Prefecture; Yin was demoted and Shu also became Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Emperor Zhaozong fled to Hua Prefecture; Cui Yin was demoted and Shu was made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 天子自岐下還宮，以樞檢校右僕射、同平章事，出為廣南節度使。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven returned to the palace from below Qi, Shu was made Acting Right Vice Director, Associate Chancellor, and sent out as Military Commissioner of Guangnan.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the palace from Qi, Shu was made acting right vice director and associate chancellor and sent out as military commissioner of Guangnan.

sentences.zh: 制出，硃全忠保薦之，言樞有經世才，不可棄之嶺表，尋復拜門下侍郎，監修國史，累兼吏部尚書，判度支。

translations.literal: When the appointment edict issued, Zhu Quanzhong vouched for him, saying Shu had talent to order the age and could not be abandoned in the Lingnan region; soon again appointed Vice Minister of the Chancellery, Commissioner for Revising the National History, cumulatively concurrent Minister of Personnel, deciding the Treasury and Expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment edict was issued, Zhu Quanzhong vouched for him, saying Shu had the talent to govern the age and should not be abandoned in the far south; he was soon reappointed vice minister of the chancellery, commissioner for revising the national history, cumulatively minister of personnel, and controller of the treasury and expenditure.

sentences.zh: 崔胤誅，以全忠素厚，相位如故。

translations.literal: When Cui Yin was executed, because Quanzhong's ties with him had long been close, his chancellor position remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Yin was executed, Shu retained his chancellorship because of his long-standing closeness to Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 從昭宗遷洛陽，駐蹕陜州，進右僕射、弘文館大學士、太清宮使，充諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: Following Zhaozong's move to Luoyang, when the court halted at Shan Prefecture, promoted to Right Vice Director, Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall, Commissioner of the Great Pure Palace, charged as Transport Commissioner for Salt and Iron of all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Zhaozong's move to Luoyang, when the court halted at Shan Prefecture, Shu was promoted to right vice director, grand academician of the Hongwen Hall, commissioner of the Great Pure Palace, and transport commissioner for salt and iron of all circuits.

sentences.zh: 哀帝初嗣位，柳璨用事，全忠嘗奏用牙將張廷範為太常卿，諸相議，樞曰：「廷範勛臣，幸有方鎮節鉞之命，何藉樂卿？

translations.literal: When Emperor Aidi first succeeded to the throne, Liu Can wielded power; Quanzhong once memorialized to appoint his guard officer Zhang Tingfan as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the chancellors deliberated; Shu said: "Tingfan is a meritorious minister; fortunately he may receive the command of a military commissioner's seal and axe—what need is there for the Music Director?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Aidi first succeeded to the throne, Liu Can wielded power; Quanzhong once memorialized to appoint his guard officer Zhang Tingfan as director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the chancellors deliberated, and Shu said: "Tingfan is a meritorious minister; he may well receive a military commissioner's seal and axe—what need is there for the director of imperial sacrifices?

sentences.zh: 恐非元帥梁王之旨。

translations.literal: I fear this is not the intent of Marshal Prince of Liang."
translations.idiomatic: I fear this is not the intent of Marshal, the Prince of Liang."

sentences.zh: 」乃持之不下。

translations.literal: Thus he held it and would not issue it.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore withheld the appointment and refused to issue the decree.

sentences.zh: 俄而全忠聞樞言，謂賓佐曰：「吾常以裴十四器識真純，不入浮薄之伍，觀此議論，本態露矣。

translations.literal: Before long Quanzhong heard Shu's words and said to his guest aides: "I always considered Pei the Fourteenth's capacity and insight truly pure, not entering the ranks of the frivolous and shallow—viewing this discussion, his true nature is revealed."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Quanzhong heard what Shu had said and told his staff, "I always thought Pei the Fourteenth was genuinely upright and above the company of shallow men—but this remark shows his true colors."

sentences.zh: 」切齒含怒。

translations.literal: He ground his teeth and harbored anger.
translations.idiomatic: He gnashed his teeth in fury.

sentences.zh: 柳璨聞全忠言，尋希旨罷樞相位，和陵祔享，拜尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Liu Can heard Quanzhong's words and soon, to please his intent, removed Shu from the chancellor position; at the joint enshrinement at Heling Mausoleum, Shu was appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can heard Quanzhong's words and soon obliged him by removing Shu from the chancellorship; at the Heling mausoleum enshrinement ceremony Shu was appointed left vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五月，責授朝散大夫、登州刺史，尋再貶瀧州司戶。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he was punished and appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Governor of Deng Prefecture; soon again demoted to Registrar of Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he was demoted to grand master of splendid happiness and prefect of Deng; soon he was demoted again to registrar of Long Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六月十一日，行及滑州，全忠遣人殺之於白馬驛，投屍於河，時年六十五。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day of the sixth month, traveling as far as Hua Prefecture, Quanzhong sent men to kill him at Baima Post Station and cast his corpse into the river; he was then sixty-five years old.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh day of the sixth month, as he reached Hua Prefecture, Quanzhong sent men to kill him at Baima Post Station and throw his body into the river; he was sixty-five years old.

sentences.zh: =【贊】=史臣曰：晉卿謹身蒞事，足為純臣，避寇全忠，固彰大節。

translations.literal: = [Appraisal] = The historiographer says: Jinqing guarded his person and attended to affairs—sufficient to be a pure minister; avoiding bandits he preserved his integrity, firmly displaying great constancy.
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal: The historian writes: Jinqing conducted himself with care and devotion in office—worthy of a loyal minister; in fleeing the rebels he preserved his integrity and displayed true greatness of character.

sentences.zh: 然博達精審，豈不知寬猛之道哉！

translations.literal: Yet broadly penetrating and finely scrutinizing—how could he not know the way of leniency and severity!
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was learned and perceptive—how could he not have known the balance of leniency and severity!

sentences.zh: 奉林甫之旨，順胥吏之意，悅附張倚，欺罔時君。

translations.literal: He followed Linfu's intent, complied with clerks' wishes, pleased and attached himself to Zhang Yi, and deceived and misled the sovereign of the time.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Li Linfu's wishes, indulged the clerks, curried favor with Zhang Yi, and deceived the emperor.

sentences.zh: 生為重臣，諂林甫之勢也；

translations.literal: In life a great minister—this was fawning on Linfu's power;
translations.idiomatic: In life he was a great minister who flattered Li Linfu's power;

sentences.zh: 歿改美謚，引元載之恩焉。

translations.literal: in death his posthumous name was changed to a fine one—this drew on Yuan Zai's grace.
translations.idiomatic: after death his posthumous name was improved through Yuan Zai's favor.

sentences.zh: 或言晉卿不為巧宦者，誠不信也。

translations.literal: If some say Jinqing was not a crafty official, truly one cannot believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Those who claim Jinqing was no crafty courtier simply cannot be believed.

sentences.zh: 冕力贊中興，名居大位，奉公抱義，可以致身；

translations.literal: Mian vigorously supported the restoration, his name occupied a great position, served the public and embraced righteousness—by this one could establish oneself;
translations.idiomatic: Mian vigorously aided the restoration and rose to high office; in serving the state with integrity he might have distinguished himself—

sentences.zh: 賣官度僧，是何為政？

translations.literal: yet selling offices and licensing monks—what sort of government is this?
translations.idiomatic: yet he sold offices and licensed monks—what kind of governance was that?

sentences.zh: 及其老也，貪冒尤深。

translations.literal: When he grew old, greed and presumption were especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: In his old age his greed grew worse still.

sentences.zh: 遵慶學術貞明，為國忠所出；

translations.literal: Zunqing's learning and conduct were upright and clear, yet he was sent out by Guozhong;
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing was learned and upright, yet Yang Guozhong banished him from court;

sentences.zh: 恭儉謹密，遇蕭華素知。

translations.literal: respectful, frugal, cautious, and secret—he met Xiao Hua who had long known him.
translations.idiomatic: he was respectful, frugal, and discreet, and won recognition from Xiao Hua, who had long known his worth.

sentences.zh: 位重行純，老而彌篤，彼二公固有慚德。

translations.literal: His position was weighty and his conduct pure; old yet more earnest—the other two lords surely had cause for shame beside him.
translations.idiomatic: He held high rank with pure conduct and grew more steadfast with age; beside him the other two men had reason to feel ashamed.

sentences.zh: 向克荷堂構，不墜門風。

translations.literal: Xiang was able to bear the hall's framework and did not let the family's wind fall.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang upheld the family legacy and did not let its reputation decline.

sentences.zh: 樞因盜而振，盜憎而亡，宜哉！

translations.literal: Shu rose through the bandit, and when the bandit hated him he perished—fitting indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Shu rose through the rebel's favor and died when the rebel turned against him—as was fitting!

sentences.zh: 君子守道遠刑，蓋慮此也。

translations.literal: The gentleman guards the Way and keeps punishment far off—perhaps he considers this.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman holds to the Way and keeps punishment at a distance—perhaps he has just such cases in mind.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：奧矣晉卿，貪哉裴冕。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: profound was Jinqing, greedy was Pei Mian.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: Jinqing was profound; Pei Mian was greedy.

sentences.zh: 遵慶父子，及之者鮮。

translations.literal: Zunqing father and sons—few could reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Few could match Zunqing and his sons.
